title: The Bear and the Travellers
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Two Travellers were on the road together, when a Bear suddenly appeared on the scene. Before he observed them, one made for a tree at the side of the road, and climbed up into the branches and hid there. The other was not so nimble as his companion; and, as he could not escape, he threw himself on the ground and pretended to be dead.
The Bear came up and sniffed all round him, but he kept perfectly still and held his breath: for they say that a bear will not touch a dead body. The Bear took him for a corpse, and went away.

When the coast was clear, the Traveller in the tree came down, and asked the other what it was the Bear had whispered to him when he put his mouth to his ear. The other replied, "He told me never again to travel with a friend who deserts you at the first sign of danger."
Misfortune tests the sincerity of friendship.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what suddenly appears while the two Travellers are on the road?
options: A pack of wolves
A sudden storm
A Bear
A group of bandits

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the first Traveller do when he sees the Bear?
options: He climbs up into the branches of a tree
He runs down the road as fast as he can
He throws a stone at the Bear
He calls out for help from nearby villagers

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the second Traveller do since he cannot escape?
options: He hides behind the same tree as his companion
He offers the Bear some food to distract it
He stands still and shouts loudly at the Bear
He throws himself on the ground and pretends to be dead

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Bear do to the Traveller lying on the ground?
options: It drags him off into the woods
It sniffs all round him and then goes away
It paws at him until he moves
It roars loudly and circles him twice

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Traveller in the tree ask once the Bear is gone?
options: How long the other man had been lying there
Whether the other man was seriously hurt
What the Bear had whispered to the other man's ear
Why the Bear did not climb the tree after him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the second Traveller say the Bear told him?
options: Never again to travel with a friend who deserts you at the first sign of danger
To always carry a weapon when travelling
To avoid this road at all costs from now on
To thank his companion for climbing the tree

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Bear leave the second Traveller alone?
options: It is frightened away by the man in the tree
It has already eaten and is not hungry
It is startled by a noise farther down the road
It mistakes his stillness for death and loses interest

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the second Traveller really saying with his answer about the whisper?
options: He is repeating a joke the Bear actually made
He is criticizing his companion for abandoning him instead of helping
He genuinely believes the Bear can whisper messages
He is warning his companion about a different danger ahead

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "nimble" mean in "not so nimble as his companion"?
options: Loud and easily startled
Brave and unafraid of danger
Quick and agile in movement
Careless and easily distracted

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: A time of danger reveals who your true friends really are
Bears are less dangerous than most travellers assume
Climbing a tree is always the safest response to danger
Pretending to be dead never actually works in real danger

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many Travellers are on the road together at the start?
options: Three
Just one
A whole group
Two

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the second Traveller do while the Bear sniffs at him?
options: He whispers quietly for the Bear to leave
He keeps perfectly still and holds his breath
He crawls slowly away while unnoticed
He grips a stick in case the Bear attacks

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when does the first Traveller come down from the tree?
options: As soon as the Bear appeared
Before the Bear had even left
When the coast was clear
Only after his companion called for him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the passage mention that "a bear will not touch a dead body"?
options: It explains why playing dead succeeds in saving the second Traveller
It explains why the Bear left the first Traveller alone in the tree
It shows that the Bear was already unwell before it arrived
It proves the Bear had encountered this trick before

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the first Traveller feel uneasy asking what the Bear whispered?
options: He genuinely believes the Bear left a hidden message
He wants to know if the Bear will return later
He is worried the Bear injured his companion somehow
He senses his own actions during the danger may be about to be judged

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "deserts" mean in "a friend who deserts you at the first sign of danger"?
options: Protects
Abandons
Follows
Warns

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Both Travellers work together to frighten the Bear away
The Bear chases both Travellers up the same tree
One Traveller abandons the other to danger, and is quietly rebuked for it afterward
The Travellers thank the Bear for leaving them unharmed
